text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Some multinationals, including Anglo American Corporation of South Africa Ltd, have agreed to sell significant fractions of their shareholdings in Zimbabwean companies to local black investors in support of a major government programme to economically empower majority blacks, President Robert Mugabe told the Herald.

He praised Anglo which earlier this year offered to sell 20 percent of its shares in Bindura Nickel Corporation to the government. The government hopes to warehouse the shares for black investors when it eventually buys them. Mugabe said the government was also talking to Lonrho to offer black managers equity in the group.
- A senior Zimbabwean government official said none of the dozens of pyramid scheme money clubs that have collapsed in the past few weeks were registered.
